nom: Clinique Clarifying Face Lotion Toner 1 - Very Dry to Dry

avis.titre: Great product, but maybe rethink the bottle?
avis.texte: This works well on my aging, dry combination skin. It isn't drying and seems to do the job of exfoliating well. More than once I've turned it over and accidentally dumped out a bunch of product because I forgot that it's just a full bottle opening. Waste of product and a mess. Add a plastic disc to the end with a small hole like other products and this would be 5 stars easily.

avis.titre: No comparison to Mild Clarifying Lotion
avis.texte: I'm trying to be polite, but I bought Clarifying Lotion 1 because it seems to be the best of the worst for my Type II skin. I used Clarifying Lotion 2 for two decades and loved it. I stopped using it when I developed rosacea and later went on retinoids, but now that my skin has fully adapted and rosacea is in full remission, I wanted to repurchase No 2. I was surprised that it is the only Clarifying Lotion out of all 6 that contains no salicylic acid—its main ingredients are alcohol and witch hazel. I don't understand why a lotion designed for dry/combination skin would include degreasing alcohols/astringents while leaving out the benefits of pore-refining, rosacea-friendly BHA. Even the lotions designed for the most sensitive skin, such as 1.0 contain BHA. I picked up Clarifying Lotion 1 only because Clinique replaced the excellent Mild Clarifying Lotion with version 1.0, which I loathe for the same reasons other reviewers dislike it. Clarifying Lotion 1 is OK, but it doesn't make my skin feel refreshed, I have noticed zero skin refinement, and I've started to see more facial redness. I also wish that Clinique would stop adding dyes to skincare. Finally, naming different products with different goals in the same line (Clarifying Lotion 1 and Clarifying Lotion 1.0) is a skincare mistake waiting to happen and provides a poor (confusing) customer experience.

avis.titre: #1 stings when applied now but never did before
avis.texte: I've been using Clarifying Lotion #1 for at least 10+ yrs now and it's never done this (see below). I always have 2 bottles on hand as backup. When I changed over to my 2nd bottle recently (2nd was bought at a later time than the first), everyday when I use it, I notice that under my eyes, on the sensitive upper cheek area, it stings when applied, burns a little and turns my skin pink and raw. It also seems to really dry out my skin (skin turns flaky and white in areas until I apply moisturizer) more than usual. I thought it might be from me using additional Clinique products for a more complete skin regimen that I've been doing recently. But none of the other Clinique products I added recently stings or does this. After reading other reviews, it seems it's likely the effects of the alcohol that others have also experienced. #1 has never done this the entire time I've used it over many years. Considered switching to 1.0 but I just don't know now. Has your ratio or list of ingredients in #1 changed recently? Can I anticipate that #1 will always do this going forward? Because if so, I can't use it anymore. I don't use anything on my face, or body, that stings, burns, or turns it red.

I really enjoy this toner. It has no scent and really does, as advertised, prepare my skin for moisturizer. I notice a difference if I don't use it before moisturizing. I've noticed an improvement in my skin's texture too. I'd buy again.
